question: What is a tissue in the human body?

options.A: An independent organ performing a single job
options.B: A collection of unrelated floating body fluids
options.C: The smallest chemical unit in the body
options.D: A group of similar cells working together

explanation: Think of a tissue as a teamwork setup! It's a collection of similar cells teaming up to carry out a specific job in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: How do tissues and body membranes connect?

options.A: Membranes exist independently without any cellular tissue
options.B: Tissues are larger structures that wrap around membranes
options.C: Membranes are thin sheets formed by combined tissues
options.D: Tissues only form inside the cavities of membranes

explanation: You've got this! Body membranes are just thin, protective sheets made by combining different types of tissues together. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which tissue type is responsible for body movement and contraction?
explanation: Whenever you move, thank your muscle tissue! It's packed with special fibers that shorten to create movement. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four main types of body tissue?
explanation: The four heavy hitters are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue. Fluid is actually just a part of connective tissue, not a separate main category! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which membrane lines closed body cavities that don't open to the outside?
explanation: Serous membranes are like inner wrappers for closed cavities like your chest and belly, keeping things slippery and safe. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: A patient has inflammation in a freely movable joint. Which membrane is affected?
explanation: Synovial membranes line our movable joints and make a slippery fluid so our bones glide smoothly without grinding. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why does the lining of the esophagus have multiple layers of epithelial cells?

options.A: To pump blood effectively through the gut
options.B: To absorb large amounts of nutrients quickly
options.C: To withstand friction from passing food
options.D: To allow fast gas exchange into the blood

explanation: Swallowing food is tough on the throat! Having multiple layers (stratified) means the top layers can get worn out and easily replaced. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: What cell arrangement is best for quick gas exchange across a tissue surface?
explanation: Keep it simple! A single, ultra-thin layer of flat cells lets oxygen and other gases breeze right through with no trouble. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient has swelling in their legs because fluid is trapped in the tissue spaces. What is this called?
explanation: Edema is just the clinical term for swelling caused by fluid building up where it shouldn't be in the body tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: As a nurse, why do you need to turn and reposition bedridden patients regularly?

options.A: To stimulate mucous membrane secretion in the lungs
options.B: To accelerate the growth of nervous tissue
options.C: To prevent pressure ischemia and tissue breakdown
options.D: To increase the production of synovial fluid

explanation: Brilliant nursing care in action! Moving patients takes the squeeze off their blood vessels, preventing tissue damage from lack of blood flow. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)
